answer: An agent market can blunt sybil attacks by charging a uniqueness deposit that unlocks only after several independently attested epochs. That deposit rests on a visible ledge: if peers catch cloned wording or coordinated voting, the stake is burned. The loss does not stop at one sockpuppet; it starts a ripple of freezes across addresses that share funding trails or near-identical answers. Influence therefore cannot vault to a zenith overnight, because cheap replica identities never survive the lock and audit window.
